The mission team has completed the final round of thermal and vibration testing on the lunar lander, clearing the way for shipment to the launch site next month. Engineers subjected the vehicle to temperatures ranging from minus 180 to plus 120 degrees Celsius over twelve days, simulating the swings it will experience during a full lunar day and night. No anomalies were recorded. "This was the last major environmental milestone before launch," said the project manager. "The vehicle performed as designed, and the data will help us refine our operating procedures on the surface." The lander will carry four science instruments, including a ground-penetrating radar that will map subsurface ice deposits near the south pole. After arrival at the launch site, technicians will integrate the vehicle with its rocket adapter and conduct a final series of electrical checks. Launch is currently planned for early spring, pending range availability and a successful flight readiness review.
